newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkey's Ciller says will not quit coalition.
newsitem.headline: Turkey's Ciller says will not quit coalition.

text.p: Turkish Deputy Prime Minister Tansu Ciller said on Tuesday she would not abandon her government alliance with Prime Minister Necmettin Erbakan.
"No," Ciller said when asked by reporters if she would quit the coalition in a row over Islamist activism.
The Milliyet daily on Tuesday quoted Ciller, a pro-Western conservative, as telling her True Path Party on Monday she would desert Erbakan if he did not heed an army warning.
The military-dominated National Security Council (NSC) ordered Erbakan at a meeting last Friday to reverse a recent wave of Islamist zeal partly encouraged by his Welfare Party.
Erbakan, the first Islamist to lead modern Turkey, has dug in his heels against the military challenge.
He attended the security meeting but the press says he refused to sign a final statement urging an anti-Islamist crackdown.
Parliament began debate on Tuesday afternoon of a censure motion brought by the leading opposition party against Erbakan's government.

There were no immediate signs that the government, with a majority of around six in the 550-seat assembly, would lose the vote. Last week the alliance survived a vote on a censure motion brought by two leftist parties that said the country's secular system was under threat.
